Subject: Post-demo: quick confirmation on volume bands & surge profile

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate the walkthrough of Stellarium’s moderation and content-enrichment flows. Per our ask during the call, can you confirm the following so I can finalize the hosted pricing estimate?

Quick asks (please reply inline):
- Expected monthly token volume (range if uncertain): e.g. 50M-150M tokens / month
- Typical tokens per API call (prompt vs response split). If you have a sample CSV, attach it.
- Peak TPS (tokens-per-second) during highest window and duration of that window (e.g., 15 TPS sustained for 2–4 hrs/day)
- Budget target: target $/1M tokens or a monthly $ target
- Latency SLA expectation (p95 gen latency target)

Attachments: redwood-pricing-proposal-v2.pdf (proposal with hosted bands + burst options)

Next steps:
1) If you can return the sample traffic CSV and ballpark ranges, I’ll produce a hosted API quote with three pricing bands and a recommended burst cap.
2) If you prefer a reserved capacity model, we’ll map the peak TPS to a Dedicated GPU pool proposal.

Thanks — copying Vanessa for any ops/contract questions.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes

Quick answers inline:
- Monthly tokens: we’re currently projecting 60M in month 1 scaling to 140M by month 6; for quoting use a 50M–150M band.
- Tokens per call: avg prompt ~140 tokens, avg response ~360 tokens => ~500 tokens per full call.
- Peak: observed peak traffic equivalent to ~22 TPS (token-level) averaged over 3-hour window in evening (US), occasional spikes to ~35 TPS for 10–15 minutes.
- Budget target: target $/1M tokens is $28–$34 (we’d like to see examples at $30/1M)
- Latency: target p95 generative latency <750ms

Attached: stellarium_usage_sample.csv (hourly token histogram for last 30 days)

Also: curious how streaming (if we switch to chunked responses) affects billing and latency — can you include notes?

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.inference>

Date: 2026-11-24T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick confirmation on volume bands & surge profile

Thanks Elena — very helpful. A few clarifications and a worked example to align on unit economics.

Worked examples (using your avg 500 tokens/call):
- Per-call token draw: 500 tokens
- Cost at $30 / 1M tokens: 500 / 1,000,000 * $30 = $0.015 per API call
- Monthly cost examples:
  • 60M tokens => 60 * $30 = $1,800
  • 100M tokens => 100 * $30 = $3,000
  • 140M tokens => 140 * $30 = $4,200

Notes on peak handling:
- For peaks (22 TPS sustained, spikes to 35 TPS), hosted API with autoscaling + burst buffer will handle the 10–15 minute spikes without requiring Dedicated. However, if you anticipate sustained 20–35 TPS windows longer than ~4 hrs/day we should evaluate a Dedicated pool for predictable latency and lower unit cost.
- Streaming: billing remains token-based; streaming reduces tail latency for long responses but can increase overall tokens if client requests additional chunks. We’ll include a streaming appendix in the quote.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm whether you want a 6-mo or 12-mo committed band (I’ll price both with step-down unit economics).
2) Confirm if the monthly band to lock is: 50–75M | 75–125M | 125–175M — pick one for an accurate contract.
3) Ops: Vanessa, can you provide a short note on SLA language for p95 <750ms (hosted) and typical request throttling rules?

I’ll produce an updated hosted quote and an alternative Dedicated sizing by EOD tomorrow once you confirm the band.

—Rafael
